stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag the cannon barrel to aim, use the $v_0$ slider to set launch speed, then FIRE. Watch the live $E_c$ gauge. Try at least two different angles and change $v_0$ to see how kinetic energy evolves.
stages.concept: Kinetic energy: $E_c = \tfrac{1}{2} m v^{2}$. Along a free trajectory, the work-energy theorem $\Delta E_c = \sum W(F_{\text{ext}})$ reduces to $\Delta E_c = W(P) = -m g \Delta z$, so $E_c(z) = \tfrac{1}{2} m v_0^{2} - m g z$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Each target shows its position $(x, z)$ and the required $E_c$ at impact. The mass $m$ is fixed and shown in the HUD. Use the preview arc to line up each shot. Deduce $v_0$ from $E_c$, then aim.
stages.concept: At a target of altitude $z_T$, the impact kinetic energy is $E_c^{T} = \tfrac{1}{2} m v_0^{2} - m g z_T$. Invert to get $v_0 = \sqrt{\,2 E_c^{T}/m + 2 g z_T\,}$. The angle $\alpha$ then chooses which trajectory of speed $v_0$ passes through $(x_T, z_T)$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No preview arc. No $E_c$ gauge. Read each target's $(x, z)$ and required $E_c$. Compute $v_0$ from the work-energy theorem, then $\alpha$ from the trajectory equation. You get one shot per target — no spray-and-pray.
stages.concept: Trajectory: $z(x) = x \tan\alpha - \dfrac{g x^{2}}{2 v_0^{2} \cos^{2}\alpha}$. If a wall of height $h$ sits at $x_w$, require $z(x_w) > h$. Two $\alpha$ solutions per target — pick the one that clears any obstacle.

labels.tip1: aim, change v₀, then FIRE — watch the E_c gauge fill and empty
labels.tip2: compute v₀ from the required E_c, aim α with the preview arc
labels.tip3: compute v₀ from E_c, then α from (x, z). One shot per target.
labels.peek_tip_energy: v₀ from energy: ½m·v₀² = E_c(target) + m·g·z(target). Solve v₀ first — angle second.
labels.peek_tip_complementary: Two angles reach the same point at the same v₀ (α₁ + α₂ ≈ 90° on flat ground). Pick the one that clears the wall.
labels.peek_tip_range_max: Range peaks at α = 45°. If (x, z) is out of reach at your v₀, no angle helps — recheck the E_c calculation.

1.1: Drag the barrel up or down to change the launch angle α.
1.2: The v₀ slider on the right sets the initial speed. Higher v₀ means more initial E_c.
1.3: Watch the E_c gauge: at the peak, gravity has done the most work against the projectile, so E_c is lowest.

2.1: For each target, read (x, z) and the required E_c. The mass m is shown in the HUD.
2.2: Work-energy theorem: E_c(target) = ½m·v₀² − m·g·z. Solve for v₀ first, then aim.
2.3: Once v₀ is set, use the preview arc to fine-tune α. Two α values may work — either one hits.

3.1: No live E_c. Compute v₀ from ½m·v₀² = E_c + m·g·z. No trial-and-error — one shot per target.
3.2: Trajectory equation: z(x) = x·tan α − g·x²/(2·v₀²·cos²α). Substitute the target coords and solve for tan α.
3.3: For any wall of height h at x_w, require z(x_w) > h. Pick the α solution that clears it (usually the steeper one).
